outcome: A person who forgot their password asks for a link, sets a new password, and signs in
acceptance_criteria: The sign-in page shows "Forgot your password?" as a link to `/accounts/recovery/` and no longer contains "Reset opens in a later release" or "Ask your administrator for help"; it still calls no recovery endpoint until the person opens the page and submits. — verify: unit (role `link` by that name; fetch spy sees no `/accounts/recovery/*` call on `/sign-in`; `grep -rn "later release" frontend/src/features/sign-in` returns nothing); mock.

`/accounts/recovery/` and `/accounts/recovery/link/` render with no `/me` call and no top bar or phone bar. — verify: unit (render `AppShell` at both paths with a fetch spy: no `GET /me`, no `GET /role-dashboard`); mock (no "My work" link).

Desktop and phone layouts match `SCR-17-desktop-reset` and `SCR-17-mobile-reset` for the ask and the "Check your email." states apart from the exceptions in Questions for the design engineer (the missing "works for 30 minutes", the added "Use a different email" button). — verify: mock, design fidelity run at 1440 and 390 wide; `grep -rn "30 minutes\|12 characters" frontend/src/features/recovery` returns nothing.
An empty address or one without "@" makes no request and shows "Enter your work email." with focus on the field. — verify: unit (no POST on the fetch spy).

The request body is exactly `{email}` with the trimmed address and `X-CSRFToken` from a session read made at submit time; `method="post"` on the form means pressing Enter never changes the address bar. — verify: unit (body keys and header) and mock (press Enter; the address stays `/accounts/recovery/`).
A 202 shows "Check your email." with the typed address, and the text and DOM are identical for a known address and `unknown@psl.example` (same snapshot). — verify: unit and mock.

Server 422 `invalid_input` shows the server message under the field; 403 `csrf_failed`, 429, a thrown network error, 500 and 503 each show exactly the specified wording, keep the typed address, never show the server `message` for non-422 and show no number or time. — verify: unit with one fixture per row; mock with scenario cookies 429, 503, 500.

After the page reads the fragment the address bar is `/accounts/recovery/link/` with no `#`; the token appears in no URL, storage (`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `document.cookie`) or console output and is sent only in the JSON body of `POST /accounts/recovery/link`. — verify: unit (spy on `history.replaceState`, storage and `console`; assert request URLs and bodies); mock (Playwright reads `page.url()` and storage after load).
The page's metadata gives `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">`. — verify: mock (`document.querySelector('meta[name=referrer]')`).

A good link (`mock-recovery-good`) shows "Choose a new password" with the two fields and "Change password"; a wrong, expired or used fixture shows the identical unusable text and links, and the text never states which reason applies. — verify: unit (snapshot equal across the three) and mock.

After the token is cleared, a reload with no fragment calls `GET /accounts/recovery/password`: it shows the form while the binding is still valid and the unusable state when not (after a completed change). No `POST /link` is sent without a held token. — verify: unit and mock (Playwright reload).
Empty password, empty confirm and mismatch show the three messages, make no request and focus the right field; the body is exactly `{new_password1, new_password2}`. — verify: unit.

Server refusals: 422 `invalid_input` with `fields` shows each message under the right field with both fields cleared; 422 without `fields` shows the callout; 422 `recovery_unavailable` shows the unusable state; 403 `csrf_failed` (a second press with the new token works without a reload); 429; 500/503 and a network error (the extra "may already be changed… try signing in" sentence with a link). The `grep -rn "12\b" frontend/src/features/recovery` shows no password rule. — verify: unit with one fixture per row; mock for the scenario cookies.

A good change shows "Your password is changed." with a "Sign in" link to exactly `/sign-in`; it is not a success callout (`tests/no-success-callouts.test.ts` passes unchanged); the page makes no `/me` or `/me/onboarding` call and does not follow any URL. Reloading afterwards shows the unusable state. — verify: unit and mock (`e2e/recovery.spec.ts`).

Passwords are never kept after the request: the form fields are empty after a failure and after success, and neither password is in the URL, storage, a rendered error or a log line. — verify: unit (spies as in criterion 8).
Rendered text is escaped: a server `message` containing `x` shows literally. — verify: unit.

Keyboard and accessibility: Tab order is field to button to link; the problem callout takes focus on a failed submit; focus goes to the heading on "Check your email." and on Done; axe finds no violations in the ask, sent, loading, ready, field-error, page-error, unusable and done states, desktop and phone. — verify: mock (Playwright with `expectNoAxeViolations`, as in `e2e/frame.spec.ts`).

The mock routes validate against the live contract (202, 200 `{ready}`, 200 `{complete}`, 422 `invalid_input`, 422 `recovery_unavailable`, 403 `csrf_failed`) and reject a non-current token. — verify: unit (extend the `tests/mock-live-me.test.ts` pattern).

F-58 is unharmed: `tests/sign-in.test.tsx` (except the forgot-password assertion changed by criterion 1), `tests/sign-in-next.test.ts` and `e2e/sign-in.spec.ts` pass; `grep -n "recovery" frontend/next.config.ts` is empty and `tests/next-config.test.ts` passes. — verify: `npm test` and the e2e spec.

Request for a real local account and for `unknown@psl.example` both return 202 `{requested:true}`; the response bodies and headers (except `Date`) are identical, and a second request inside the cooldown also returns 202 with the same body. — verify: live (`curl` through the proxy comparing bodies; browser shows the same page).

A real link opened in the browser: `POST /link` returns 200 `{ready:true}`, the address bar loses the `#`, the form appears, and `GET /password` returns `{ready:true}` before and after a reload. — verify: live (network log and `curl` with the cookie jar).

A tampered token, a random 80-character token and a token for another account's consumed request each return 200 `{ready:false}` and the page shows the identical unusable state; no other account's data appears. — verify: live.

A password refused by the server (shorter than the server minimum, or one on its common list) shows the server's message under the field and leaves the link usable; the page's own code contains no number. A mismatch is stopped by the page. — verify: live; `grep -rn "12\b" frontend/src/features/recovery` empty.

A good password returns 200 `{complete:true}`; the same link opened again shows the unusable state and `POST /password` without a binding returns 422 `recovery_unavailable`; signing in on `/sign-in` with the old password gives 422 `sign_in_failed` and with the new password succeeds. — verify: live (`manage.py shell` shows `check_password` true for the new password).
A missing or wrong `X-CSRFToken` on `POST /request`, `/link` and `/password` returns 403 `csrf_failed` and changes nothing (the link still works afterwards). — verify: live (`curl`).

An expired link (move the delivery row's `created_at` back past the server's limit in `manage.py shell`) and a link whose account route or password changed after it was sent both give the unusable state. — verify: live.
Race: two tabs set a good password with the same link; one gets Done, the other the unusable state, and exactly one change is recorded (`consumed_at` set once). — verify: live.

The link in the emailed message (read from the delivery record or the local mail backend) opens the page without the page redirecting through a Django route; if its host is not the frontend origin, record it under the backend leftovers (A-54) without changing the PR. — verify: live and a note in `build.md`.

risk.rationale: RISK is high. This is account recovery: the token lives in the URL fragment, a password change is hard to undo, and mistakes can enable account takeover or user enumeration (D-SIGNIN r2, D-AUTH r3, contracts/psl-factory.openapi.json 1.22.0). SURFACES are ui, api, security and auth. I left out contract-change because it only edits the F-58 page link, and product-decision because the unknown rules are bound out of scope. Add the Opus security reviewer under D-180.
